title: Remove the middle feeder from a packed pick-and-place feeder rail
instruction: Take the middle feeder off the rail and lay it on the blue mat. Leave the other two feeders in place.
context: Robot builders assemble their motor-driver and sensor boards on pick-and-place machines such as the desktop LumenPnP, and every board change means swapping tape feeders on the machine's rail; the same changeover is routine on SMT production lines. The feeders sit side by side at the rail's slot pitch, 0.5 mm apart, so no finger fits beside the middle one, and once tipped out of line it drops back into its sprung catch unless held. A neighbour knocked off its slot loses its place.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the bench top: x forward, y to the robot's left. Lot A (the screenshot): a 100 mm length of black 20 x 20 mm V-slot aluminium extrusion lies along x from x 190 to 290, its centre line at y -60 and 112 mm above the bench, screwed to two black aluminium feet (10 x 20 mm posts on 26 x 60 x 6 mm plates) at x 195 and 285 that are clamped to the bench. On its left face sit three printed yellow PETG slot blocks (14.5 wide, 6 thick, 26 tall) at x 224.5, 240 and 255.5, each with a 5 x 5.5 x 6 mm alignment peg. On them sit three Opulo LumenPnP 8 mm tape feeders (front, middle, back at x 224.5, 240, 255.5; 15.5 mm slot pitch, an estimate): a black body 15 x 158 x 42 mm resting on the rail top and reaching to y -200 (the pick end), a hook nose in the slot along the rail's top face, a clip either side of the peg, a yellow sprung release lever with two teeth under the slot block, and a spool arm holding a white 7 inch (178 mm) component reel, 13 mm wide, centred at y +65 and 97 mm above the bench, with dark wound tape. Each feeder with its reel is 0.29 kg (estimate). A blue anti-static mat, 300 x 420 x 3 mm, 0.5 kg, lies centred at (350, 360). Lot B moves the mat to (320, 360); everything else is as in lot A. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Part drawings: README and fixture/.
scoring: Judged from the videos and photos, with a ruler. 0 at any moment, and it stays 0: either outer feeder is knocked loose (moves more than 5 mm at its hook on the rail, or tips more than 10 degrees); any feeder is dropped (its body moving faster than 1.2 m/s, as in a free fall from about 7 cm) or leaves the bench. At the end: 0 if either outer feeder sits more than 2 mm (at its hook) or 3 degrees from where it started, or any part of the middle feeder is within 5 mm of the rail, its feet, a slot block or a peg. 0.5: the middle feeder is 5 mm or more clear of all of them (held, moving, or not lying on a side). 0.75: it also lies on one of its broad sides, within 20 degrees of flat, resting on the bench or mat (lowest point within 5 mm of it), with no gripper within 5 mm, still for 1 s. 1.0: as 0.75, and all of it lies inside the mat's outline. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz) per trial
reset_notes: 1. Lift any loose feeder clear and lay the mat flat at its lot position (lot A centre (350, 360) mm; lot B (320, 360)). 2. Check the rail's feet are still clamped on their outlines marked on the bench. 3. Mount each feeder in its slot: hold it with the reel end high, set its hook nose into the slot on the rail's top face, swing the reel end down until the clip straddles the peg and the yellow lever clicks under the slot block. 4. Check each feeder body rests flat on the rail top, the reels hang free 8 mm above the bench, and the reel tape is wound tight. 5. Check with a spring scale that a few newtons pressed down on a feeder's pick end tips it out of its catch, then reseat it. 6. Move both arms to their rest poses.
fidelity: Feeder envelope, 15 mm width, rail and 7 inch reel follow the maker's CAD and documents. The hook, clip, peg and lever are simplified boxes and cylinders sized from photos; they, the 0.29 kg mass, 15.5 mm pitch and lever spring (releasing at a few newtons on the pick end) are estimates. The reel is fixed to its arm (no spin, no loose tape) and there are no electrical contacts. The two lots move the mat: they stop one fixed habit, not a memorised replay.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B, 0.0 and 0.0: it reached toward the bank but did not move the middle feeder); demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0, each in about 640 of the 2,400 steps). Simulation runs with object_jitter=0; no physical trials.
